relevance_note: Single case report of a boy with CD18-complex deficiency confirmed by FACS and immunoprecipitation ("Ileocolitis in a patient with CD11/CD18 leucocyte glycoprotein deficiency"); in scope by diagnosis, although no ITGB2 variant is reported.
method_note: Read the whole paper; built the JSON with a short Python script holding values I transcribed by hand, then checked every span verbatim. The converted text interleaves two printed columns (abstract, case report line beginning 'A bone ileal mucosa', Discussion), so sentences are split; I quoted only contiguous fragments and used span lists where a statement is split (e.g. CD11/CD18 deficiency confirmation by FACS/immunoprecipitation, EGD findings, stridor/hypoxaemia, Pseudomonas aeruginosa tracheitis, 'No pseudomembranes'). Because of the column interleaving the order of the hospital course is partly unclear (which admission the EGD, ileal and colonoscopy findings belong to); feature onsets were left null there. No gene, no ITGB2 variant and no genetic testing are reported (diagnosis by protein expression only), so the variants table is empty; LAD type is not stated in those words. The patient was described before as 'patient 1, reference 13' (Wright et al. 1990); label is 'patient' (rule 5) since this paper gives no own label. Typical LAD features listed in the abstract/introduction (delayed umbilical cord separation, septicaemia, gingival disease) are general statements about reported cases, not about this patient, and were not used. Not used for the checklist: 'ulcerated lesions of the skin' (not described as necrotic or pyoderma gangrenosum-like), positive blood cultures (bacteraemia, not called sepsis), Rebuck skin window (not stated as absence of pus), immunisation-site lesion (vaccine type not stated). 'gastroenteritis' at three months was taken as a gastrointestinal infection for the checklist; stool pathogens and C difficile toxin were negative during the colitis work-up. Normal immunoglobulins and complement recorded as excluded abnormalities (D-27). Vital status 'alive' rests on 'He has remained symptom free for over a three year follow up'. Post-transplant resolution (normal mucosa on repeat colonoscopy) not recorded as excluded features since it describes later resolution. No contradictions found.

treatment_summary.value: multiple antibiotics; granulocyte transfusions for pseudomonas tracheitis; mesalamine (Asacol, 30 mg/kg/day) with metronidazole; allogenic bone marrow transplantation at 7 years of age with peritransplant BCMU, cyclophosphamide, VP-16 and ARA-C, then oral cyclosporine and prednisone for six months, tapered over the following six months
span: antibiotics were unsuccessful in eradicating the pseudomonas infection until granulocyte transfusions were administered
Treatment with mesalamine (Asacol, 30 mg/kg/day) was started, along with metronidazole
a bone marrow transplantation was performed at 7 years of age

Immunosuppressive therapy given in the peritransplant period included BCMU (300 mg/m² intravenous once), cyclophosphamide (35 mg/ kg/d intravenous for four days), VP-16 (100 mg/m² every 12 hours intravenous for four days), and ARA-C (100 mg/m² every 12 hours for four days).
Cyclosporine (5 mg/kg) and prednisone (1 mg/kg) were administered orally for the first six months, and then tapered gradually over the following six month period.
